News.title: Fears of ISIS resurgence in Iraq as US forces pull out from last bases – as experts warn move will ‘benefit’ Tehran
News.content:
Next

FEARS are mounting of an ISIS resurgence as a US-led coalition formed to fight marauding jihadists is pulling out of Iraq.

Footage shows a convoy of US tanks leaving Iraqi Kurdistan earlier today, marking the official end of Operation Inherent Resolve – after 12 years in the Middle Eastern country.



And the remaining 2,500 troops have now left the territory, giving some hope to Iraqis.

But security experts warn that the withdrawal could give Iran and its allies free rein, while also allowing a comeback for ISIS.



“Iran stands to benefit strategically from the coalition’s departure because it removes a military presence that for years acted as a counterweight to Iran’s influence in Iraq,” said Jasim al-Bahadli, an Iraqi security analyst.

He predicted that pro-Iranian militia groups would not only portray this as a victory – but “seek to translate that momentum into greater influence over security and political decision-making”.

Abu Mojtaba al-Yasiri, a commander in Iraq’s Islamic Resistance, the group of Iran-backed armed factions, hailed the withdrawal ⁠as “a historic victory for the Iraqi Islamic resistance groups… and a crushing defeat” for the US.

He said: “Iraq has proven that its sovereignty cannot be secured by foreign forces, but by the resistance and the will of its people.”

In 2014, a US-led coalition began a campaign of airstrikes in Iraq and Syria after the capture of large swathes of the countries by ISIS.

Having terminated the US occupation of Iraq only three years earlier, the then-President Barack Obama decided to send troops back to prevent the group from expanding.



At their height, fighters occupied a ‌third of the country and slaughtered thousands of people.

Kurdish commander Sirwan Barzani warned that now – amid a lack of US intelligence, logistical support and drones – ISIS could regroup.

He said: “For more than two ⁠weeks, we have noticed movement by sleeper cells, after it was announced in the general media that there will be an official withdrawal of the international coalition from Iraq by the end of September.”



“This has boosted, in my opinion, the morale ‌of the fighters.”

Iraqi security forces said a suspected ISIS cell was preparing suicide attacks to coincide with the pullout.

The plot highlighted concerns that the militant group ‌remains capable of exploiting security gaps despite years of military setbacks, said four Iraqi security and ​army officials.

Colonel Khalid al-Bayati, a senior security official in the strategic oil town of Kirkuk, said the group “is seeking to send a message that it is powerful and capable of launching bloody attacks.”

Iraq had also linked the end of the military mission to the disarmament of the numerous armed group and paramilitaries it hosts.



Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said last week that the new deadline to do this was June 30, 2027.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But some have given no indication that they will follow through with the plan.

Alina L. Romanowski, fellow at the Atlantic Council, said: “The hardest-line armed groups – Kata’ib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba and Kata’ib Sayyid al-Shuhada – have so far given no indication that they are prepared to surrender their weapons to the state and integrate into Iraq’s armed forces.”

News.title: Thousands of French students clash with cops & hurl projectiles in nationwide riots – as hundreds of teens arrested
News.content:
Next

THOUSANDS of French students have clashed with cops and hurled projectiles in nationwide riots – with hundreds of teenagers arrested.

Furious pupils torched bins, unleashed fireworks and battled riot police as as protests erupted outside schools across France on Tuesday.



At least 440 people – most of them minors – were detained as the school revolt descended into violent clashes.

Some protestors even hurled hydrochloric acid at officers in seven terrifying incidents, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez.



A staggering 48 members of the security forces were injured as cops fought back with batons and tear gas.

Nuñez told BFMTV: “We don’t have the final tally yet, but I’m told two thirds [of detainments] led to police custody.

“Violence is never legitimate. There is nothing that justifies violence.

“There is nothing that justifies showing up at institutions to demonstrate, masked, with your face disguised, carrying projectiles, and waiting for the intervention of law enforcement just to go after them.”

The chaos erupted as thousands of pupils protested over crumbling schools, overcrowded classrooms, gruelling timetables and a shortage of teachers.

Around 400 schools were reportedly hit by riots, while teaching was completely halted at more than 40 lycées – the French equivalent of sixth-form colleges.



Violence flared from Rennes and Bordeaux to Lille and the Alpes-Maritimes as the movement spread far beyond its origins around Paris.

In the capital’s communist-run suburb of Malakoff, dozens of teenagers clashed with police after fireworks were set off near a railway station.



Protesters screamed “la jeunesse est dans la rue” – “youth is in the streets” – as smoke and the deafening blasts of fireworks filled the air.

One stunned resident in neighbouring Vanves warned: “Watch out, there’s a riot.”

In Lille, dramatic scenes showed rubbish containers ablaze outside a school, while clashes were also reported between police and pupils in Lyon.

Up to one in ten high-school entrances in Paris were reportedly blockaded.



Masked youngsters perched on dumpsters outside the Arago school beneath a placard reading “Macron explosion”, while another banner at the Hélène-Boucher school declared: “Fewer cops, More money.”

The latest mayhem came just a day after a teenage protester was blasted in the face with a police grenade launcher from close range during another school blockade.

Horrifying footage from Saint-Ouen-l’Aumône in Val-d’Oise shows the youngster confronting riot police outside the Château d’Épluches vocational school on Monday.

The footage shows an officer appearing to strike at the teenager before the youngster kicks towards the cop’s abdomen.



Moments later, an officer fires a projectile from a Cougar grenade launcher at close range, striking the boy in the face and sending him crashing to the ground.

The stricken teenager is seen clutching his face before other youngsters rush over and drag him away.

His devastated mum later told Le Parisien his mouth had been “torn apart.”

“All his upper teeth have been broken…We don’t know yet what’s left of his lower teeth,” she said.



The teenager suffered several broken teeth and was taken to hospital in Pontoise.

Two investigations have since been opened into the explosive confrontation – including a probe by France’s police watchdog into the officer’s use of the launcher and another into alleged violence against a police officer.

Trade union chief Sophie Binet branded the footage “extremely shocking” and called it an act of “police brutality.”

She said: “These events must be fully investigated and the necessary sanctions imposed.



“If high school students want to mobilize, they must be able to do so, and the conditions must be in place to allow them to express their demands.

“We cannot teach them about democracy at school and then, when they want to express themselves in a democracy, send the police after them,” Ms Binet said.

The school rebellion has been gathering pace since last week, with pupils furious over budget cuts to education.

The Union Syndicale Lycéenne said the protests were fuelled by a “shortage of teachers and staff, dilapidated schools, overcrowded schedules and classes”.



It blamed “ten years of Macron’s policies and the lack of resources in the national education system”.

But the spiralling violence has triggered a bitter political row over the protests.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu acknowledged that problems inside French schools “must be heard and addressed”, while fiercely condemning the violence surrounding some blockades.

He said on X: “Pupils have a right to safety. Staff have a right to protection.

“Police officers have a right to respect when carrying out their duties. The difficulties in the lycées must be heard and addressed.



“Violence must be condemned unequivocally and those responsible held to account.”

Hard-left France Unbowed leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon, meanwhile, accused the government of a brutal crackdown.

“The students … are harmless,” he said on social media.

“The Lecornu government has ordered repression. This brutality is irresponsible and has a clear racist undertone.”

The turmoil erupted on the same day thousands of firefighters, teachers and other public-sector workers joined a nationwide strike over pay and looming budget cuts.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

More than 5,000 firefighters were reportedly given pride of place in a Paris march after crews complained that this summer’s ferocious wildfires had exposed shortages of equipment and manpower.

The unrest heaps fresh pressure on Lecornu’s government as it attempts to push through its 2027 budget in a hung parliament.

News.title: Woman loses both her legs after bungling doctors mistakenly amputate WRONG limb in botched surgery, lawsuit claims
News.content:
Next

AN ELDERLY woman has lost both her legs after a surgeon confused her right and left sides, it has been alleged.

Sharon Jacks, from Ohio, is suing a doctor at Selby General Hospital after the planned below-the-knee operation on her cancer-plagued right leg left her as a double amputee.



The surgical team had multiple chances to spot the grave mistake when draping the wrong leg and placing a pneumatic tourniquet on the thigh, according to a 32-page lawsuit.

Brad Layne, the lawyer for the 74-year-old victim, insisted that disasters like this one “should never happen.”



“There is simply no excuse,” he told WCHS Channel 8.

“Complete and total failure by multiple medical professionals caused this catastrophe.



“Despite several opportunities to identify the mistake and stop the procedure, the surgical team somehow never noticed they were operating on the wrong leg.

“Every day for the rest of her life, Sharon must live with the consequences of those failures.”

Layne explained that the surgeon marked the correct leg before the start of the operation.

As a result of the critical misstep, Sharon “suffered severe physical injury, permanent disability, pain and suffering, emotional distress, humiliation, loss of enjoyment of life, medical expenses…,” according to the lawsuit.



Selby General Hospital told The Sun that the medical staff involved “were

held accountable for their actions and are no longer in their positions.”

“In September 2025, an adverse surgical event occurred at Selby General Hospital,” a statement said.

“At that time, our team responded immediately to address the medical needs of the patient involved and provide support to their family.

“Our proactive review of what took place confirmed this was an avoidable event, and that our expected operating room procedures were not followed.”

Wrong-site surgeries – including the catastrophic mistake of amputating the wrong limb – are classified as entirely preventable “never events”.



Studies estimate that they happen in roughly 1 in 112,000 to 1 in 113,000 general surgical procedures.

Cases of amputating the wrong limb are rare but there have been similar incidents in the past.

In 2021, a surgeon in Austria amputated the wrong leg of a patient – with the mistake only discovered two days later.

It was identified during a routine bandage change and the elderly man was told he would have to have his other leg amputated as well.

News.title: Nigel Farage ‘firebombing suspect was caught on CCTV but cops failed to spot him’ – as police watchdog launches probe
News.content:
Next

THE culprit who “firebombed” Nigel Farage’s property last year was caught on CCTV – but shockingly escaped cops’ notice, a report claims.

Met Police wrongly informed the Reform UK leader that CCTV had failed to capture the suspect behind the attack at his home in April 2025.



A police watchdog has now launched a probe into the incident, with Scotland Yard admitting they had missed the opportunity to “protect the public”, according to the Telegraph.

Counter-terrorism police only realised the blunder after they reviewed the footage for a second time, following Ann Widdecombe‘s shocking murder in July, which sparked fears about politicians’ security.



Cops discovered the attacker and their car had in fact been captured in the recording “over an extended period” of time.

The staff member originally tasked with examining the footage has now been placed under investigation by the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).

The watchdog is evaluating whether the staff member may have failed to review the footage to the “standard required” and in turn, endangered the public.

To date, no one has yet been charged with the attempted firebombing.



Commenting on the error, Mr Farage claimed it was Ann’s tragic murder at her Dartmoor Bungalow in July that prompted the IOPC investigation.

He said: “It’s a great, great tragedy that it took the death of Ann for the security services in Britain to finally take seriously the safety and security of Reform politicians and Reform prominent figures.”

“Up until that moment, we had been treated very differently to everybody else.”

He said that while the cops’ self-referral was “unprecedented”, he was nevertheless confident that the counter-terrorism team were now taking the job “seriously”.

At the time of the incident, police believed that it was an attempted burglary gone wrong and the case was closed – with no arrests made.



The Reform UK leader reported a “lit incendiary device” being shoved through his letterbox during the attack.

Over a year later, on August 7, police admitted that they had neglected a “relevant” line of inquiry during their initial review.

A source said at the time: “There has been a very serious policing error which is why counter terror police have referred themselves to IOPC, which is unprecedented.”

Reform UK’s deputy leader Richard Tice said: “Only recently have the authorities woken up to the abuse and intimidation I and other Reform MPs have had, despite plenty of real examples that we have provided.

“For too long, the threats we have faced have not been taken seriously.



“The fact that the police have referred themselves to the IOPC speaks for itself. They recognise that they’ve messed up.”

It comes as Mr Farage received a record-breaking £72million in donations from two crypto billionaires in just 48 hours.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Reform UK leader said the money would go towards investing in the party structures ahead of a general election.

News.title: True story of Bridget Sullivan: Irish servant at heart of Lizzie Borden case & how Netflix twisted relationship
News.content:
Next

THE Irish maid who found herself caught up in the Lizzie Borden murder mystery became one of the most important witnesses in one of America’s most notorious murder cases.

But Bridget Sullivan’s real story is very different from the one now playing out in the new Monster series on Netflix.



Bridget, played by Vicky Krieps, is seen encouraging Lizzie, portrayed by Ella Beatty, to murder and becomes romantically involved with her in scenes which experts say are pure fiction.

Bridget was the Borden family’s live-in maid and had worked at their Fall River, Massachusetts, home for almost three years when Andrew and Abby Borden were brutally murdered on August 4, 1892.



On the morning of the killings, Bridget was outside washing the windows when Abby was murdered upstairs.

She was speaking to the maid next door over the fence as she worked and later went upstairs to take nap in her own third-floor bedroom.

Bridget then heard Lizzie screaming and came downstairs, where Andrew was found bloodied on the sofa after reportedly being struck 11 times.

Abby’s body was later discovered in an upstairs guest bedroom after suffering 19 blows to the head.

Bridget was questioned by investigators and later gave evidence at Lizzie’s trial in June 1893 after she was accused of killing both her father and stepmother in a case that quickly became a national sensation.

But due to the lack of evidence, Lizzie was ultimately acquitted after the jury deliberated for around 90 minutes.



No one else was ever prosecuted for the deaths, leaving the case unresolved and spawning countless theories about what really happened.

And the real Bridget was very different to the one portrayed on screen.

Historian Dr. Stefani Koorey previously told The U.S. Sun there is no historical evidence that Bridget and Lizzie were lovers, describing the romantic storyline in the Netflix series as “completely fabricated.”



She also said the show misrepresents Bridget’s duties inside the Borden home, as she did not clean Lizzie or her sister Emma’s bedrooms.

That is backed up by Bridget’s own testimony at Lizzie’s 1893 trial, when she said her work consisted of “washing, ironing and cooking and sweeping,” while the Borden daughters took care of their own rooms.

Bridget was a young Irish immigrant who crossed the Atlantic alone to build a new life in America.

At Lizzie’s trial, she gave her age as 26 and said she had been in the United States for seven years, placing her arrival at around 1886, although historical records differ over her precise year of birth.

She first settled in Newport, Rhode Island, before moving to South Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, and eventually making her way to Fall River.



Bridget told the court she had no parents, brothers or sisters in America, although she did have other relatives in the country.

She initially worked for a woman she identified as Mrs. Reed before joining the Borden household around November 1889.

By the time Andrew and Abby Borden were killed on August 4, 1892, Bridget had worked for the family for two years and nine months.

On the morning of the murders, she was washing windows inside and outside the Borden home before later going upstairs to rest.

After Lizzie’s acquittal, Bridget eventually left Massachusetts and moved west to Anaconda, Montana.



There she married Irish-born John M. Sullivan in 1905, with Koorey’s research indicating the couple had no children.

John died in 1939, while Bridget later lived in Butte, Montana.

Despite her central role in one of America’s most notorious murder cases, Bridget largely stayed out of the public eye didn’t attempt to capitalize on her connection to the Bordens.

There is also no reliable evidence that Bridget and Lizzie maintained a relationship after the trial, and no known correspondence between the two women has emerged.

Koorey also claimed family she spoke to had no idea she was “that Bridget Sullivan.”



One enduring legend claims Bridget made a deathbed confession suggesting she had withheld information or changed her testimony to protect Lizzie.

But the alleged confession was not documented at the time and only emerged secondhand years later, with Koorey saying there is “zero evidence” Bridget ever made such an admission.

Bridget died from cardiac failure at a hospital in Butte on March 25, 1948, with arteriosclerosis – a thickening of the arteries – also listed on her death certificate.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She was buried alongside her husband at Mount Olivet Cemetery in Anaconda.

Lizzie remained in Fall River after her acquittal, living at her mansion Maplecroft and dies years earlier in 1927 at the age of 66.

News.title: Sick beast jailed for having sex with HORSES in vile animal abuse ring sparks fury after opening PET SHOP in Scots town
News.content:
LITTLE SHOP OF HORRORS Sick beast jailed for having sex with HORSES in vile animal abuse ring sparks fury after opening PET SHOP in Scots town







Next

A SICKO jailed for having sex with horses is now running a pet shop, we can reveal.

Jordan Turnbull, 33, is on the sex offenders register for vile acts with two Shetland ponies.



But council bosses granted him a licence to sell exotic fish in Armadale, West Lothian, sparking fury among locals.

One outraged customer said: “I felt ill when I found out who he was.”



Horrified locals have vowed to boycott the pet shop which was opened by the perv after he served a jail term for having sex with ponies.

In a sick twist, depraved Turnbull even named his new business after an ancient goddess known as the “mistress of horses”.

read more sun stories BEAST MOVED Paedo ex-world snooker champ Graeme Dott 'targeted in prison' over sick crimes



And despite still being on the sex offenders list, council chiefs gave him a licence to sell animals in Armadale, West Lothian.

Turnbull is one of the three directors of exotic fish specialist Astarte Aquarium.

But when a worried mum told of her fears about taking her kid there, the firm put out a message insisting he wasn’t a threat because his conviction was for “acts with horses, nothing more”.

The aquarium gets its name from Astarte, worshipped in the Middle East more than 3,000 years ago as a goddess of “sexual love, war and power” — and was often depicted riding horses naked.



One local said: “This has to be a very sick joke, surely? But no one is laughing about it. I felt sick when I found out who he was.”

An angry ex-customer hit out: “I have no idea how a man convicted of having sex with an animal and put on the sex offenders register got permission to open a shop which deals with looking after and selling animals.

“What is even more messed up is he’s named the pet shop after a Greek goddess known for loving horses.”

Another added: I’ve been in there plenty of times — never again.”

A third said: “Abuse is never funny. And depravity rarely stops with one victim group, in this case animals.



“What this monster did is unbelievably cruel. He caused real-life damage and horror.”

Turnbull was appointed as a director of the firm last October ahead of the store’s opening.

In 2021 he was caged for seven months after he confessed to being part of a horse sex abuse ring, along with another two men.

Turnbull molested ponies Jack and Ruby over three months at an Aberdeenshire farm.

He admitted an “unnatural connection” with the animals and was convicted of bestiality.



At the time he claimed his business, Newton Don Nurseries, would go under if he was locked up. It was dissolved the following year.

One of the company’s bosses was Kieran Brown, 27, who is also listed as a director of Astarte.

Turnbull was added to the sex offenders register for a decade, so will remain on it until 2031.



Last night a mum who visited the pet store with her kid hit out: “The fact remains that he’s still on the sex offenders register.

“I’ve had my child in the shop with me. How can anyone deem this acceptable?” Turnbull has been seen on social media posts with two Great Dane dogs that have been described as “shop mascots”.

News of his conviction spread on social media this week.

The shop then issued a statement on their own Facebook page.

It said: “We are not going to hide from the fact this happened.



“The matter went through the criminal justice system several years ago and the sentence imposed by the court was served.

“Astarte Aquarium was established afterwards.

“We ask people to judge us on the business we operate today — the welfare and standard of care provided to the animals in our shop, the condition of our premises and the contribution we try to make to our community.”

A spokesman revealed discussions were “ongoing” about axing Turnbull from the business but added: “Removing a director of a company cannot be done instantly.”

In response to the concerned mum who’d taken her child into the pet shop, the spokesman said: “SOR status doesn’t automatically involve kids. He is on the register for acts with horses, nothing more.”

We revealed in 2022 that Turnbull was working as a coach driver.

West Lothian Council was approached for comment.

News.title: One of UK’s biggest mosques BANNED from sponsoring foreign workers over ‘migrant job ruse’
News.content:
MOSQUE BAN One of UK’s biggest mosques BANNED from sponsoring foreign workers over ‘migrant job ruse’







Next

ONE of the UK’s biggest mosques has had its licence to sponsor immigrant workers revoked by the Home Office.

The mosque’s leaders had backed visa applicants by vouching for their employment.



But investigators heard allegations that applicants did not work at the mosque — and that some paid cash in “visa scams”.

The Sun is aware of three people permitted leave to stay in the UK after being sponsored as “ministers of religion” by Hounslow Jamia Masjid and Islamic Centre in West London.



One worked as a school admin assistant; another at a legal firm connected to a mosque trustee; and a third at a wholesale butcher’s in Heston, West London, near Heathrow.

The mosque has denied any wrongdoing and is challenging the Government’s decision.



Last year, The Sun revealed the Charity Commission is investigating claims of misuse of more than £1m and corruption at Hounslow Jamia Masjid & Islamic Centre.

Worshippers made a series of damning allegations to the government watchdog – and provided documents to our reporters.

Probes were also launched by Hounslow Council and the Labour Party into individuals said to have a “stranglehold” over the community.

Simmering tensions within the mosque amid accusations of harassment, abuse, intimidation and violence erupted in a major brawl and police and an ambulance were called.



A trustee of the mosque resigned his position after 20 years of service, including 10 years as chairman.

A councillor reported five alleged attacks on his home and car to cops and begged the council and Labour big-wigs to step in.

In his damning resignation letter from the mosque Abdul Majid told how when he ran the Hounslow Jamia Masjid the bank balance was consistently between £400,000 to £500,000 in credit.

Mr Majid reported to investigators: “Unfortunately the current financial state of the mosque is a cause for great concern, with the account balance now very low.

“This, among other matters, has compelled me to conclude that I can no longer continue in this role in good conscience.”



Around £300,000 of charitable donations collected each year at the mosque “do not appear in any official accounts or bank records”, it was claimed.

Mr Majid referred to documents in which the firm BNP Paribas Leasing Solutions filed a claim for £150,000 against the mosque’s 11 trustees in a row over a 12-year lease of photocopiers.

An out of court settlement – “without full board approval or proper discussion” – means the mosque is paying the company £5,000 per month until August 2027.

Mr Majid added: “Furthermore, it has come to my attention that some trustees have employed their own relatives under the mosque payroll, allegedly for the purpose of supporting visa applications.

“These individuals are not actively working at the mosque.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This deeply undermines the ethical standards we are meant to uphold as custodians of a sacred institution.

“Additionally, decisions such as awarding sponsorships to relatives of trustees have been made without prior discussion or consent of the board.”

News.title: Drunk flyer attacked Heathrow security boss after downing cocktails before long-haul flight to India
News.content:
Next

A DRUNK flyer attacked an airport security chief after downing cocktails before a long-haul flight.

Bhavna Hirani, 42, yelled “who the f*** are you” at passengers as she tried to find her seat on a Boeing 787 Dreamliner.



The prosecutor added: “She was continuously swearing at cabin crew and passengers.

“Flight attendants and passengers tried to calm her down, but she shouted: “Who the f*ck are you? I want to get to my seat.”



She was seen swaying as she was escorted off the Air India flight from Heathrow to Mumbai.

Panicked Heathrow security led the woman off the packed jet and told her to calm down.

But Hirani continued to abuse “terrified” staff, and was seen throwing paper cups of orange juice.

She then twice hit a female security official trying to calm her down in April’s incident.

The yob was arrested by Heathrow cops by the departure gate, where she told officers she had drunk cocktails.

Hirani, of Barnet, North London, pleaded guilty to assault and entering an aircraft when drunk.



She got a 12-month community order with 60 hours of unpaid work and alcohol monitoring and a £349 fine.

Hirani told Uxbridge magistrates she was upset at messages from her brother over a family wedding.

She said: “It was out of character.”

News.title: River Wear - latest: Three teens dead after car plunges into water in Sunderland
News.content:
Three teenagers have tragically died after a car entered the water in the River Wear in Sunderland - a boy who survived has been arrested

Three teenagers - two boys and a girl - have died after a car smashed through a barrier and plunged into a river.

The vehicle careered out of control and entered the River Wear in Sunderland shortly before 1.30pm. Four people are understood to have been in the black Audi A3 at the time, with a 17-year-old boy managing to reach safety. He is currently in hospital with what have been described as non-serious injuries and has now been arrested in connection with the incident.

Northumbria Police said the three bodies had all been recovered from the water. Chief Superintendent Scott Cowie, Area Commander for Sunderland, said: "This is a truly tragic incident where three young people have lost their lives. Our thoughts are with their families, friends and all those impacted by what has happened.

"We will continue to support them in any way that we can and ask that their privacy is respected at this time. I want to thank all of our partners who supported the multi-agency search efforts."

A huge search and rescue response included an HM Coastguard search and rescue helicopter, the Great North Air Ambulance Service and the North East Ambulance Service's full Hazardous Area Response Team.

Pictures from the scene showed emergency services lining the riverbank, where a section of metal railing has been damaged.

News.title: Trump announces AI firms sign deal to ‘self police’ tech and claims 'data centres will be very popular'
News.content:
Trump announces AI firms sign deal to ‘self police’ tech and claims 'data centres will be very popular'

The President has announced the deal with the leaders of America's largest AI firms, and said he believes controversial data centres will become 'very popular' in the future

View 3 Images US President Donald Trump and Mark Zuckerberg, chief executive officer of Meta Platforms Inc., speak to members of the media following a meeting with tech executives on artificial intelligence at the White House in Washington, DC, US, on Tuesday, Sept. 29, 2026. The gathering follows a surge in concern about AI potentially posing a threat to humans. Photographer: Tierney L. Cross/The Washington Post/Bloomberg via Getty Images (Image: © 2026 Bloomberg Finance LP)

The leaders of the world's largest AI companies have signed up to an 'accord' to 'self-police' the technology, President Donald Trump has announced.

‌



The accord will include internal and external reviews, Trump said during a meeting at the White House aimed at addressing Americans’ fears about the technology . He also claimed data centres will become 'very popular' in the future.

‌



The deal comes after AI companies have faced questions over the safety of the technology, as the 'Godfather of AI' said earlier this month there was 'a 10 percent chance' it could wipe out humanity in the next decade.

‌



“I think I’m seeing tremendous self-policing. And they understand that they have to self-police,” Trump told reporters during an impromptu press conference outside the West Wing.

Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson met leading executives from top tech firms that are spending hundreds of billions of dollars to build out AI infrastructure, including data centres in communities across the country that have sparked grassroots, bipartisan opposition. The group included CEOs who have called for a slowdown in the development of the technology after several high-profile incidents where AI agents have gone rogue.

View 3 Images US President Donald Trump speaks to members of the media following a meeting with tech executives on artificial intelligence at the White House (Image: © 2026 Bloomberg Finance LP)

‌



The accord, which Trump posted on his social media site Truth Social late Tuesday (September 29), opened the door to future regulation but focused on four voluntary steps for the companies to take.

The accord said the companies would implement “robust internal controls,” partner with an “independent external auditor” to assess whether the controls were working, and set up a committee among each company’s board of directors to evaluate reports from internal and external auditors.

“Over time, it may make sense to codify these steps into laws and regulations,” the accord said. Trump repeatedly praised the business executives for developing a technology that he said would produce “unbelievable growth.” Investment in data centres and the accompanying computer equipment has accelerated the economy and boosted the stock market, which has swelled investment accounts for higher-income Americans and lifted their spending.

‌



Yet there were some notes of caution on Tuesday. Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, who has been one of the most outspoken voices calling for a slowdown in the development of AI, said “the technology has very real risks.”

“And, you know, the mechanism, how we address those risks is still under discussion,” Amodei said. The accord was signed by Trump, Amodei, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and Elon Musk as founder of xAI, which is now part of SpaceX.

Trump suggested there would be about 10 people named to a committee to “watch over the whole enterprise” and said the accord would be “morally binding.” He also said he would name someone to oversee the agreement in coming days after consulting with industry.

‌



Huang sat to Trump’s right during a White House luncheon meeting, according to a seating chart the president posted on Truth Social. Musk sat to Trump’s left.

Earlier on Tuesday, Trump promised that the US government would not limit the development of artificial intelligence or support calls for “guardrails” or other restrictions.

“I will never stifle the growth of a technology that will be bigger than the industrial revolution,” Trump said at the unveiling of an AI chatbot, America.gov, intended to help Americans navigate government services. “We can’t stifle it, and we’re leading by a lot.”

‌



The unveiling of the AI government chatbot occurred at a daylong event in Washington during which multiple Trump administration officials celebrated a “Golden Age” fuelled by what Trump insists on calling “super intelligence,” rather than artificial intelligence. Secretary of State Marco Rubio highlighted that the chatbot at America.gov could soon be used to apply for a first-time passport fully online, without an in-person visit to a processing centre that is currently required.

Trump also said the executives had agreed to assuage the bipartisan opposition to data centres cropping up in local communities across the country, by providing more financial support to local schools or taking steps to reduce energy costs.

View 3 Images Victoria Derbyshire left speechless by 'Godfather of AI's' warning (Image: BBC Newsnight)

‌



“You’re going to see, data centres are going to be very popular,” Trump said. If the opposition continued, Trump suggested, “they’ll be forced to go overseas or other locations.”

Also Tuesday, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in a television interview that the company is increasingly focused on safety. The day before, his company halted the rollout of a new model over safety concerns.

“We are pacing our progress, which includes sometimes not training a model,” he said on CNBC. “We have to do these in a way where we can make very confident safety cases and claims, so that people don’t have a bunch of anxiety.”

Article continues below

For his part, Trump on Tuesday portrayed the race to develop AI as largely a global competition between the United States and China, with the U.S. in the lead. He said there would be a winner and a loser, with no “second place.”

The two countries agreed last week to establish a channel for handling AI-related incidents during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington. But Trump underscored Tuesday that he didn’t want to cooperate too much with China: “I didn’t want to do anything, because we’re leading. Why would I want to do anything?”

News.title: Former American Idol star Caleb Flynn sobs as he is found guilty of murdering wife
News.content:
Former American Idol star Caleb Flynn sobs as he is found guilty of murdering wife

Former American Idol star Caleb Flynn has been found guilty of murdering his wife by shooting her twice in the back of the head as she slept - with their children in the house at the time

View 4 Images Flynn sobbed in court when the verdict was announced (Image: Court TV)

Former American Idol star Caleb Flynn has been found guilty of all counts of murder of his wife, Ashley Flynn.

‌



Flynn sobbed when th e jury in his murder trial reached its verdict on Tuesday (September 29). The 40-year-old now faces up to life in prison without the possibility of parole, and will learn hit fate at a sentencing hearing on October 5.

‌



He was found guilty of all nine charges, namely one count of aggravated murder, three counts of murder, two counts of felonious assault, and three counts of tampering with evidence. Prosecutors alleged that Flynn killed his 37-year-old wife by shooting her twice in the back of the head, and staged the scene to make it look like a burglary gone wrong , reports The Mirror US .

‌



Flynn had pleaded not guilty to the nine charges, claiming an intruder killed his wife during a burglary. Ashley had been shot twice in the back of her head while she was asleep in bed in their residence in Tippy City, Ohio, on February 16.

The couple shared two daughters, who were asleep in the house when the crime occurred. Flynn's lawyers claimed that he was asleep at the time of the shooting and had woken up to the sounds of the gunshots while he was in their daughter Ava's room.

View 4 Images Flynn's mugshot when he was charged (Image: Miami County Sheriff Department)

‌



Prosecutors said hours before Caleb called 911, he had texted his former mistress, "I choose you. I'm free. Actions will come tomorrow."

The former mistress, Alleigha Botner, had testified in court for over two days. The 24-year-old testified that Caleb told her he intended to talk to Ashley about divorce on February 16, and she thought his phrasing, "Actions will come tomorrow," meant that.

‌



When Botner learned his wife was dead, she told the court, "My heart started pounding. In my mind, it seemed like too much of a coincidence that the day he's divorcing her, she's just dead all of a sudden."

She stated that she had once thought she loved Caleb, but when the prosecutor asked her to label her feelings for him now, she replied, "I hate him." When asked about the shift of her emotions, she explained in court, "Because I believe that he murdered his wife."

Botner additionally testified that she met Flynn in 2022 while interning at their church, and their sexual relationship occurred for about a year, starting in May 2024. She noted that she knew he was married.

‌



In Botner's testimony, she said that Flynn would regularly voice that he wanted Ashley "gone" or "dead," and that he referred to her as "d-----bag," "wh-re," "sl-t," and "spawn of Satan."

View 4 Images Caleb Flynn appeared on American Idol season 12, in 2013 (Image: American Idol / YouTube)

"He said that he wishes if he could kill her and not go to jail or get arrested -- I forget exactly what he said -- that he would do it," Botner testified.

‌



She read some of their over 100,000 text message exchanges, in which Caleb expressed wanting Ashley dead.

One of those texts Caleb sent to Botner in August 2025 read, "I was up until 4 a.m. last night ... trying to think of ways to kill her and not go to jail. If I could literally kill her and not go to hell, I would do it in a heartbeat."

View 4 Images Caleb Flynn murdered his wife Ashley (Image: Facebook)

‌



In one July 2025 text, Botner read, she had mentioned wanting to kill Ashley. She cried as she read it, saying she regretted the message and she "didn't mean it."

In another text to Caleb in August 2025, Botner had stated that she wanted him to divorce Ashley and not kill her.

"I'm not asking that you take her life, obviously, because that's not what you should do, and I know you actually wouldn’t," she wrote. "But to make the divorce happen, it would change everything."

Article continues below

Botner was not charged in the case nor accused by authorities of any crime. She also told the court that she had not been offered anything for her testimony.

News.title: Man City charges LIVE: Premier League's damning statement, 'sham' contracts, City respond
News.content:
The latest news on Manchester City's charges after the club were found guilty of alleged breaches of Premier League financial rules

Welcome to our live blog on the latest Manchester City charges news, with the latest updates after the club were found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League rules.

While the Premier League remain silent on the situation, City have spoken out a couple of times.
