News.title: Taylor Swift becomes most-awarded artist in MTV history
News.content:
Taylor Swift broke records at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards (VMAs) on Sunday, becoming the most-awarded artist in VMA history.

The pop star, 36, was previously tied with Beyoncé for the title, with 30 VMAs each. However, Swift took home three awards at the ceremony, bringing her career total to an unmatched 33.

The Fate of Ophelia, ⁠Swift’s first single from her record-breaking The Life of a Showgirl album, claimed the top trophy – Video of the Year – and she dedicated the honour to the late country music legend Dolly Parton.

During her speech, Swift praised Parton as “the ultimate showgirl” who told stories that were “so vivid and so rich”.

“I think that we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time,” she said.

Parton, an award-winning country singer, died in August at the age of 80.

Swift also received the inaugural Artist Director Honors, a new award meant to recognise artists “whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling”.

The 36-year-old has written and directed 18 videos of her roughly 60 videos during her career. The ‌most recent, for ‌her new single Patient Zero, debuted during ⁠the ceremony.

News.title: Five reasons why Australia’s win over Boks was an all-time classic
News.content:
If the Wallabies play like this in their own backyard at their own World Cup next year, boy we are in for a treat. After years in the doldrums, this five-try victory over South Africa was the latest reminder of their transformation under the stewardship of Les Kiss.

Their gritty performance in Perth – the city where Australia will open rugby’s showpiece in 12 months’ time – was caveated by the fact they were facing a second-string Boks side. But there can be no denying they are on an upward trajectory, even if their discipline dramatically deserted them late on.

In a helter-skelter denouement, Australia played the majority of the final 10 minutes of the match with 11 men on the pitch as South Africa threatened to mount a late comeback. Tom Wright’s eye-catching intercept try looked to have secured a match-winning moment, but it was scratched off after Hunter Paisami joined Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan and Joseph Sua’ali’i in the bin.

Ox Nche’s 80th-minute score made it a four-point game with time left for the restart, but Australia had enough fight to secure a dramatic victory largely built on execution and patience.

Five tries by the hour mark, including a Len Ikitau first-half double, ultimately gave South Africa a mountain to climb. The Wallabies’ field coverage and industriousness in defence was far superior to that of the four-time world champions, while Max Jorgensen and Sua’ali’i were pillars of excellence out wide.

After clinching a 3-1 win over New Zealand in their historic “Greatest Rivalry” series, Rassie Erasmus had the luxury of resting several of his A-listers for this one-off Test in Western Australia. The changes ultimately had an adverse effect, with the visitors faulty at the set-piece and lacking their usual snarl and bite. They found themselves playing catch-up in a chaotic game that Australia, despite their discipline creaking in the dying moments, deserved to win.

Here, Telegraph Sport explores five reasons why this was one of the craziest Test matches in recent memory.

Wallabies outmuscle Boks over 60 emphatic minutes

The Wallabies front up impressively to earn a seven-point lead at the break after a quickfire Len Ikitau double cancels out tries from Johan Grobbelaar and Edwill van der Merwe, before Ben Donaldson finishes a sublime attacking set from the hosts.

News.title: England show ODI depth in thrashing of Sri Lanka
News.content:
England’s international summer comes to an end at the Oval with a series decider against Sri Lanka. After England won the first game in Durham, Sri Lanka bounced back to take a 16-run win at Headingley on Thursday to set up this winner-takes-all match today. Sri Lanka put up a much better fight in the second one-day international than they have throughout the rest of their white-ball tour. The tourists posted 321 for six, with their captain Kusal Mendis leading the way with 121 off 100 balls, his seventh ODI century.

England’s reply got off to the best possible start, with both openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett hitting fifties. It appeared to be going well for England, with Jos Buttler and Will Jacks also registering half centuries, but Buttler’s hamstring injury in addition to the regular loss of wickets meant Sri Lanka were able to claim victory to take us to a series decider in London today.

“I am so happy winning and getting the hundred,” Mendis said. “The overall performance was very good. We started really well and the middle order batted really well. Nothing special, basic cricket and I was very happy with 320, we wanted more than 300 on this pitch. [Dunith] Wellalage bowled really well, the whole team, after the powerplay. The guys gave 100 per cent. Today [Thursday] is finished and now we have to focus on the next game and do the basics right.”

When Buttler retired hurt in the 38th over of England’s run chase, the hosts were 254 for four and were in a great position to chase the total down and claim a series victory. From the 37th over onwards, England were only able to score one four and one six.

“It was an outstanding game,” England captain Harry Brook said. “You can look back and dwell on some many different areas but that is not what this team does, we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the Oval. We put up a really good fight with the ball. To restrict them to 320 and have the chance to chase that down was a hell of an effort.

“The lads got the chase off to a flyer. You could not really ask for much more. We probably stalled in that middle period and lost a few too many wickets, but the fight we showed was great. We have got a great opportunity now to try and win this series, and a great opportunity for 12 months’ time. In pressure situations, like the one that awaits us at the Oval, it will be great to see where we are as a team.”

Buttler has been ruled out of this match due to a hamstring injury and has been replaced in the squad by Dan Lawrence, who had been playing for Surrey in the final round of the County Championship.

Play from the Oval will get under way at 10.30am.

News.title: Saracens storm Leicester to launch new Venter era in style
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Gallagher Prem meeting as Leicester Tigers host Saracens at Welford Road.

Last season, Leicester reached the play-off semi-finals in Geoff Parling’s first full season at the club, before losing to arch-rivals Northampton Saints, who went on to win their third title in the competition.

In a new era for Leicester as they plot a route back to the very top, Aaron Wainwright and Mako Vunipola make their Prem debuts.

Leicester head coach Geoff Parling is brimming with excitement ahead of this tasty match and has talked about his side’s preparation for the new season.

“Firstly we are looking to evolve our game, we’re not looking to rip it up and completely restart,” he said. This team is built on being competitive and winning, we’ve got to be in the mix every year. For me it’s all about being consistently near the top and then getting in those big games and having the ability to perform in them.”

“I’m well aware that there’s lots of elements from the season and different circumstances but the main thing is that the league is designed to have a top four that go into the play-offs so the top four is the aim.”

Saracens finished one place below Leicester in the previous campaign and missed out on the play-offs after a 32-12 final round loss to Exeter Chiefs.

Boss Joe Shaw has handed debuts to Tomos Williams and Alfie Barbeary, and he’s raring to go ahead of this fixture.

“We’ve had a great pre-season, but we’re itching to get stuck into the league campaign now,” he said. “We have a really competitive squad who are driving standards and good habits across the pitch. We are confident in the squad we have put together and are excited to see what they can achieve this campaign.”

Kick-off is at 15:00.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon quickly backtracks on Trent Alexander-Arnold comment in live ITV interview after England win over Czechia
Sports.content:
Next

ANTHONY GORDON appeared to suggest Trent Alexander-Arnold “probably should’ve played more for England” – before quickly backtracking.

The 25-year-old put on an impressive performance as England cruised to a 2-0 win over Czechia.



He also added to his international goal tally, heading home a cross from Alexander-Arnold just moments into the second half.

Gordon was asked about the inclusion of the full-back – who made his first start for the Three Lions in almost two years – after the match.



And in response, he said: “I make that run time and time again and only a certain number of players have got that ability, technique and bravery to be willing to make the mistake trying that pass, so credit to Trent.

“That’s why he’s so good and I’ve been dying to play with him for that reason.”

The former Newcastle ace then began to say that Alexander-Arnold should’ve played more, but quickly changed the discussion.

It came following the suggestion from many fans and pundits that the Real Madrid superstar should have been included in Thomas Tuchel‘s World Cup squad.

He continued: “He’s had his own journey with England.

“Probably should’ve played… Would’ve liked to have played more than he has, sorry, but he’s been a great character during this camp, I’ve really enjoyed being around him.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

On his return to the England squad, Alexander-Arnold said: “Amazing, it’s always an honour to represent my country. It’s been a long time but I’ve always believed I can play for England.

“That belief has always been there and it was about proving it at club level. The manager gave me a chance, hopefully he is happy with how I played.”

He also went on to say it was “great” to play with Gordon.

The full-back added: “It’s a great compliment and it’s great to play with him.”

England next face Croatia on Saturday before another meeting with Czechia.

Sports.title: Man Utd legend Roy Keane tells Man City ‘cheats’ to ‘stick Premier League medals in the BIN’ after guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Next

ROY KEANE has told Man City stars to “stick their Premier League medals in the bin’ after the club’s bombshell guilty verdict.

City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Prem’s financial rules in a shock statement on Tuesday.



The Etihad club have always denied any wrongdoing and continued to stress their innocence in response.

It is not clear what sanctions the club will face, but a hefty points deduction and EXPULSION from the league have been suggested.



There have even been some claims that City could be stripped of their trophies due to the seriousness of the 130 charges.

City won three Prem titles during the period of investigation from 2009 to 2018, as well as two FA Cups, four League Cups and the Community Shield.



Pundit Keane was scolding of the club, claiming they had been “cheating” and that the City players should feel let down.

He told ITV after England‘s win over Czechia: “They knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they still done it.

“And if I was a player with the success of the last few years – I’d 100 per cent be sticking those medals in the bin.

When asked by host Mark Pougatch if players would feel let down by the club, he replied: “100 per cent you would. It’s cheating.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“You’re hearing nonsense from ex-players saying they won on the pitch. But it was cheating. There was cheating going on.

“It’s tough for the players, the manager. You’ve got owners who are quite happy cheating.

“It’s very difficult going forward for these players to maintain the level of excellence.

Keane’s fellow pundit Ian Wright called the owners’ actions “terrible” after the “unprecedented” news.



He added: “[City owners] have told them that nothing bad’s going on. If you’re a player, something’s not right there.

“It’s unprecedented what we’re seeing right now. But in respect to the owners and what they’ve done. Terrible.”

The Prem’s bombshell statement reported findings from an independent commission, which alleged the club hid £900million in “sham” commercial deals.

It claimed City “systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade”.



The club have until October 2 to launch an appeal against the findings.

City said they were “disappointed and surprised” by the commission’s findings and would be “relentless” in fighting the case.

Its statement read: “Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, that has been published today.

“The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted.



“Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

“The Club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete.”

Sports.title: Former Tottenham star breaks unwritten football rule against Spain as fans fume ‘game’s gone’
Sports.content:
Next

LAMINE YAMAL and ex-Tottenham star Ivan Perisic angered fans after breaking an unwritten sacred rule and swapping shirts at half-time.

Barcelona superstar Yamal, 19, led Spain to a dominant 4-1 victory over Croatia in the Nations League with two goals.



Marc Pubill and Nico Williams scoredthe other two at the Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan Stadium.

But fans were left raging after the first half when they noticed the star winger and PSV Eindhoven star Perisic, 37, exchanging jerseys before making their way down the tunnel.



That led to a number of football fans – who insist this custom should only take place at full-time – storming social media in anger.

One echoed Sean Dyche‘s famous quote: “Game’s gone.”



Another commented: “WHAT’S THE MEANING OF THIS?”

A third wrote: “STFU!”

This fan said: “This needs to stop.”

That one added: “Come on!!!”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

And a comment read: “What the…?”

This controversial practice has become quite regular with many others doing the same in recent years.

Only last summer Arsenal’s Declan Rice and Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe did the exact same thing in the World Cup’s third-place play-off between England and France.

Estevao Willian secured the shirt of childhood hero Lionel Messi at the interval when Palmeiras and Inter Miami faced off at the Club World Cup in 2025.



Former Real team-mates Casemiro and Luka Modric swapped shirts during the 2022 World Cup in the quarter-finals when Brazil faced Croatia and drew criticism.

There was also a famous incident way back in 2012 when then Arsenal ace Andre Santos got Manchester United legend Robin van Persie’s shirt as the two teams went back to the dressing for their half-time oranges.

Sports.title: Labour set to U-turn on plans to lift ban on footie fans drinking booze in stands
Sports.content:
Next

LABOUR is set to U-turn on plans to lift the ban on footie fans drinking booze in football grounds.

Andy Burnham earlier this month said he wanted to see beer return to the stands.



Alcohol on the terraces was outlawed in 1985 to address football hooliganism.

The PM said he did not think it was fair “for football fans to be singled out in that way”.



But Mr Burnham has reportedly been advised by police that clubs would need to pay thousands more in security costs if the ban is overturned.

Advice from Whitehall said cops had complained that they did not have the money to police games if the ban was overturned, SkyNews reported.

It comes after the PM appeared to double down on his view that supporters should be allowed to drink booze and watch footie in-person.

He previously said: “I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different.

“And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination.

“There are different ways it could be done.



“It could happen on a trial basis.”

Mr Burnham, an Everton supporter, added that he did not see how it was fair that supporters of different sports were treated differently to match-goers.

Fan groups initially welcomed the move to lift the 41-year-old ban which could bring in thousands of pounds of revenue to smaller clubs.

The Football Supporters’ Association said it was wrong to “criminalise football fans for having a pint”.

But public opinion is firmly against Labour changing the law to allow pints in the stands.



More than 50 per cent of Britons believe it would make watching football matches worse, while only 15 per cent thought it would improve their experience.

Sports.title: Three points from England’s win over Czechia as Gordon just gets better and whether Trent Alexander-Arnold keeps place
Sports.content:
Next

ENGLAND got their Nations League campaign up-and-running with a 2-0 win over Czechia.

Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane got their names on the scoresheet as the Three Lions bagged all three points in Prague.



The goals came after Czechia had been reduced to ten men thanks to Pavel Sulc’s first half red card.

Ahead of facing Croatia on Saturday, SunSport looks at three key points from England’s win.



GORDON REACHING NEW LEVEL

First of all, it was a brilliant performance from Gordon. The Barcelona winger, 25, is getting better with every week.

I didn’t think England played particularly well against ten men, but he was outstanding.

And since the World Cup knockout stages, Gordon has been at a different level.

I don’t see anyone budging him from that spot on the left-hand side of the attack.

I’m sure Gordon will be keeping his starting role against Croatia on Saturday.

KANE IS THREE LIONS’ GREATEST

Where do we start with Kane? He scored his 87th goal in 123 appearances in an England shirt.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

I’m sure he will equal Peter Shilton’s record against the same team back at Wembley.

Kane, 33, is without a doubt one of the greatest players – or I think the greatest player – this country has ever produced.

TRENT COMES ALIVE AFTER BREAK

Trent Alexander-Arnold is an interesting one when it comes to his role with England.

It was his first start for Three Lions chief Thomas Tuchel and his first start at right-back for nearly two years.

Eight other players have played in that position and I didn’t think he played very well against Czechia until the start of the second half.



Just 68 seconds after the break, he delivered a brilliant pass for Gordon to score with a stooping header.

Alexander-Arnold, 27, was better after that, so it will be really interesting to see whether he features again for England over the next two games.

But my feeling is that, despite that bright second half, he will probably be back on the bench against Croatia on Saturday. It’s one to keep an eye on.

Sports.title: Scotland 0 Switzerland 3: Horror Hampden start for Pocognoli as Swiss run amok after early Jack Hendry red card
Sports.content:
Next

SWITZERLAND are a nation from the Alps.

But at Hampden it was Scotland who were given a mountain to climb.



Jack Hendry’s early red card gave Sebastien Pocognoli’s side an uphill challenge they just couldn’t cope with.

And by time up, they were gasping for air.



The Belgian said he wanted to make the Tartan Army feel alive again inside this old ground.

But his Nations League hopes against Switzerland were virtually DEAD and buried after just eight minutes on the clock when Scotland were reduced to ten men.



Ricardo Rodrigues, Nico Elvedi and Zeki Amdouani made the extra man count with three goals which saw them earn all three points.

For Pocognoli, it’s now onto North Macedonia for their next clash on Saturday.

It’s easy in hindsight to say what Hendry should have done in the all important incident with eight minutes on the clock.

But as he trudged off the park and up the tunnel after being shown a straight red card by the Serbian ref, he would have been wishing he had dealt with the situation differently.



OUR BEST FREE BETS & SIGN-UP OFFERS

It wasn’t an easy position to be in.

Henry initially didn’t have the pace to catch the rapid Nottingham Forest star in a foot race.

But when Ndoye cut across him, Henry had two options to choose from which were better than the one he went with.



He could have slid in and made a genuine attempt to make last-ditch challenge.

And had he not won the ball to save the day, it would have been a yellow card offence.

Or he could have let Ndoye run through and take his shot. Maybe Angus Gunn would have saved it. But even if he’d scored, Scotland wouldn’t have been reduced to ten men.

Instead, Hendry took the worst option of all by giving the frontman a shove on the back.

The ref initially pointed to the spot to award a penalty – flashing a yellow card at the Scotland centre-back – before a VAR check showed the contact was outside the box, and the foul deserved a red.



The Tartan Army booed the decision but it was absolutely the right call. Hendry knew it as he headed towards the tunnel.

The fact the Swiss had a free-kick and not a penalty was supposed to be the thing that went Scotland’s way in that moment.

But when your luck’s out, your luck’s out.

Because Swiss star Rodriguez beat Angus Gunn from outside the box as though it was a spot kick.



It was the last thing Pocognioli needed.

In fairness, it was a brilliant move right through the middle the pitch which cut his team open.

That’s the risk the Belgian is taking when he sets up his team to press the game so high.

But Hendry didn’t have the legs to deal with it and it’s got to be a worry going forward with so many lightning quick attackers playing at international level in the modern game.

Could Gunn have done better at the free-kick?



That’s another thing. Because the new San Jose Earthquakes No1 looked none-too-clever as the ball flashed past him. He thew his right hand at it but clawed at thin air.

Gunn did have a couple of decent saves in the first-half but he’ll probably feel he should have done better with the first goal.

It initially felt like the game was done and dusted right there and that.

That ten-men Scotland had no hope against the 14th ranked team in the world.



But you know what, Pocognoli’s side did just fine for the rest of the first-half even though they were a man down.

There was a couple of near things in the Swiss box which gave the Tartan Army hope.

The Scotland supporters felt like they got nothing from official, Nenad Minakovic, though.

When Oli McBurnie went down after bursting forward off the right touchline, they screamed for a foul and a possible penalty.



But the truth is that the Hull City star was guilty of playacting. McBurnie threw himself to the ground when he should have stayed on his feet and tried to score or set someone up.

He did brilliantly to get away from his man, too. And generally McBurnie had a good half with his link-up play a good outlet.

When he was substituted around the hour mark, the home fans rightly applauded his efforts.

By then, though, it was 2-0 Switzerland.

Murat Yakin’s side had doubled their lead after 55 minutes with Elvedi beating Gunn with a really cute finish after the ball was recycled at a corner.



Pocognoli made other changes to try and spark something in the final half hour.

But Scotland lost their threat from middle to front with tiredness slowing them down.

Ben Gannon-Doak went on along with Ryan Christie and Robbie Ure, with Nathan Patterson and Billy Gilmour following McBurnie off the park.

But it was just asking too much of the substitutes to turn the game around with the Swiss cruising to victory.

Ndoye almost made it 3-0 in 65 minutes but was denied by Gunn who blocked with his right foot.



But with nine minutes remaining, Amdouni rifled through his hands with a blasted shot.

Like the first goal of the night, the Scotland goalie was beaten far too easily.

Sports.title: Cheeky Greece fans taunt Germany with X-rated willy chant in style of Norway’s Viking row during Nations League win
Sports.content:
Next

GREECE fans brutally trolled Germany during their historic Nations League victory by copying Norway’s famous Viking row, with a twist.

The Greeks spoiled Jurgen Klopp‘s home debut as his national team’s manager with a 1-0 victory on Sunday in Augsburg.



This was the Euro 2004 winners’ first ever victory over the four-time world champions after losing seven of their previous ten meetings.

Liverpool legend Klopp’s first ever outing in front of his compatriots went up in flames on 74 minutes when Arsenal star Christos Tzolis set up Dimitris Kourbelis up for a fine finish.



But it wasn’t just Ivan Jovanovic’s men who went viral as the fans also found a way to steal the show from the stands in quite an inventive – yet risqué – manner.

The Greece faithful borrowed Norway’s popular gimmick from last summer’s World Cup that saw fans and players rowing in unison while Manchester City superstar Erling Haaland banged the drum.

But the Greeks added their own special element that included two syllables from a very R-rated word from their own language.

The away end replaced the famous roar with that naughty Greek word that is slang for “penis” and added an X-rated gesture to boot.

The hilarious incident left fans in stitches as they stormed social media after the Nations League upset.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS



One supporter joked: “Very civilised…”

Another commented: Greeks do it better.”

A third wrote: “I could hear it on TV!”

This fan said: “We can be quite the devils when we want to…”

That one added: “Sharing our culture….”



And a comment read: “If they come to Greece and score four goals then don’t be surprised…”

Sports.title: England ratings: Anthony Gordon new darling of Three Lions faithful as Saka can’t quite link up with Alexander-Arnold
Sports.content:
Next

IT was a routine victory for Thomas Tuchel here in the Czech capital – and one that never looked in doubt after Pavel Sulc’s 25th-minute red card.

Anthony Gordon was without a doubt the star man, looking a threat all night and nodding in the opener.



It would be generous to say it was an exciting England display, more a professional one as they wore down the ten men.

But there were other notable performances, including the return of Trent Alexander-Arnold after more than a year and yet another goal for Harry Kane.



Here’s how SunSport’s Tom Barclay rated Tuchel’s players in the Fortuna Arena.

James Trafford: 6

THE second of his two-game trial as No1, Trafford had little to do after Sulc’s early red card, barring an assured late parry to repel a rare attack.



The Czech fans chanted “Please get a goal” in the second half but a first clean sheet in seven for the Three Lions never looked in real jeopardy here after the dismissal.

Trent Alexander-Arnold: 7

HIS assist 68 seconds into the second half was, in a nutshell, the argument for playing Trent for England.

Which other right-back in world football could produce a cross like that? Yes, he may give the ball away at times, yes, he may not be the best defensively, but that wand of a right foot can be a match-winner.

Trevoh Chalobah: 7

FORCED to intervene twice in a minute when the Czechs had 11 men and were looking threatening.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

First, the Como star headed away a dangerous cross with attackers lurking and then, after Kane had been robbed of the ball, Chalobah made a superb block from Sulc.

Marc Guehi: 5

ENDURED a nervy night against Spain on Saturday and overhit an early pass here past Chalobah and straight out of play.

Once the Czechs went down a man, though, it was a comfortable evening for the Manchester City defender, who presumably has a lot on his mind right now.

Lewis Hall: 7

HAD a nice understanding with Anthony Gordon down the left-hand side which came to the fore as the ten-men Czechs began to tire.

Should have scored after a one-two with his ex-Newcastle team-mate but fired agonisingly wide.



Elliot Anderson: 6

SINCE his England debut a year ago, no player has played more minutes in our national team.

The dependable midfielder missed an early clearance which led to Sulc’s chance and was then caught high by the Lyon man on the ankle, prompting the game-changing red card.

Myles Lewis-Skelly: 6

TAKEN off at half-time on his eighth cap, having been cautioned in the 35th minute for catching Lukas Cerv.

Wasn’t playing particularly badly but with the Czechs baying for a second yellow, it made sense to replace him.

Bukayo Saka: 5

LESS synergy with Trent down the right as old team-mates Gordon and Hall had down the left.



Trent hitting Saka in the back of the head with a cross at one point almost underlined that point. Helped wear Czechia down without making them pay.

Morgan Rogers: 6

UNLUCKY to hit the post with a first-half shot and full of running but nowhere near as impactful as Jude Bellingham was against Spain.

Rogers looked like he genuinely would take the No10 shirt in Autumn last year but the pecking order is clear to everyone now.



Anthony Gordon: 8

THE new darling of the England fans who sang his name here just like they did against Spain.

Gordon had talked about his football IQ being underappreciated in the build-up to this game and his header for the breakthrough was a smart one.

He has been on fire for his country ever since the knockout stages of the World Cup and is a certain starter now.



Harry Kane: 7

IT had been an uncharacteristically quiet – and at times sloppy – night for the captain… and then he did what he always does.

Goal No87 in 123 caps came with his final kick of the game before being replaced, as he seized on a loose ball and drilled it home with his left foot.

SUBS

Eberechi Eze (on for Lewis-Skelly at HT): Came on tasked with helping break ten-man Czechia down and helped do that. Denied a late goal by a good save. 7

Rio Ngumoha (on for Saka at 71): Eager to take players on with his dancing feet. An exciting prospect. 6

Jude Bellingham (on for Kane at 71): Took the armband when coming on for Kane but by then the job was done. 6



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Alex Scott (on for Anderson at 70): Came on for his debut and was busy. 6

Morgan Gibbs-White (on for Gordon at 81): Ditching his Dubai holiday was worth it as he picked up another cap here, filling in on the left-hand side. 6

Sports.title: Humphries, Wade progress at World Grand Prix as Rock dumped out
Sports.content:
Luke Humphries was not punished for a raft of missed finishing doubles as he beat a below-par Dave Chisnall to reach the second round of the World Grand Prix in Leicester.

Humphries - who has made the last three finals in this event, winning in 2023 ahead of two runners-up finishes since - is the new favourite to triumph this year following defending champion Luke Littler's shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night.

Cool Hand, sporting a scab on his forehead he put down to an allergic reaction, defeated Chisnall 2-0 while averaging only 80.41 and going at 26 per cent on his doubles as he secured a second-round meeting with Chris Dobey's conqueror Jermaine Wattimena.

Image: Humphries will take on Jermaine Wattimena in the second round on Thursday evening

Chisnall had a chance to break Humphries and push for a deciding set only to bust his score, before the world No 2 wrapped up victory on double four and then appeared to shush someone in the crowd.

Dobey was one of two seeds to tumble on Tuesday evening, alongside Josh Rock, who fell to Niels Zonneveld as the Dutch debutant peeled off three ton-plus finishes in the third set to book a last-16 date with Gary Anderson.

Rock - who at one point attempted an audacious 101 finish with bullseye, one, bullseye - had lit up proceedings by following a 180 with a roof-raising 151 to break Zonneveld and ensure a deciding set.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Rock produced six brilliant darts to win the second set against Niels Zonneveld before losing in a decider

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rock took a unique route as he attempted a checkout of 101, leaving Sky Sports' Wayne Mardle with a lot to say!

Dobey, meanwhile, suffered a first-round exit for the third year running.

'Hollywood' - who burned four darts to break Wattimena in the opening leg - averaged below 80 and really struggled to hit the mandatory starting double in legs, with a sizzling 128 finish at the start of the second set his only moment of magic as he lost 2-0.

Wade progresses but more Grand Prix woe for Heta

James Wade fought back from a set down and shrugged off six missed match darts in the space of two visits to beat Joe Cullen 2-1 as he resumed his bid for a third Grand Prix title and first in 16 years.

A key moment came in the fourth leg of the second set when Wade hit the bull for a finish of 81, just as Cullen was eyeing a break that would have left him throwing for victory.

Wade faffed about before getting over the line, squandering arrows at double top and double 10 in the third leg of the deciding set before pinning double 10 in the next to advance.

Image: James Wade won the World Grand Prix in 2007 and 2010

Wade's reward is a clash with Stephen Bunting, who defeated Andrew Gilding 2-1 in the final match of the round.

There was further Grand Prix despair for Damon Heta as he suffered a sixth-straight first-round loss - the Australian has never won a match here - after surrendering a one-set lead and wasting a match dart at double five in the second set against Anderson.

Anderson, runner-up in 2016 to Michael van Gerwen, swept the third set 3-0 while averaging 110.

Gian van Veen saw off fellow Dutchman Dirk van Duijvenbode in straight sets for his first victory on this stage after round-one exits in 2024 and 2025, to Ross Smith and Littler respectively.

However, Van Duijvenbode missed two tries at double 16 to set up a decider having belatedly found his scoring form after an abject display while losing the first five legs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player William O'Connor took out 95 with two double 19s against Ryan Searle in their World Grand Prix clash

Van Veen will play Ryan Searle next after 'Heavy Metal' punished four missed match darts from William O'Connor to progress as he won the final three legs of their encounter having lost the previous five.

O'Connor's electric run after losing the first set included taking out 95 with back-to-back double 19s but the Irishman - appearing at this event for the first time in over a decade - then lost his way.

Sports.title: Gordon-inspired England seal much-needed win over Czech Republic
Sports.content:
Pavel Sulc's first-half red card helped England recover from a nervy start to register an Anthony Gordon-inspired 2-0 Nations League win over the Czech Republic in Prague.

While the Three Lions toiled in the early stages and nearly fell behind twice to presentable chances wasted by Sulc, Barcelona winger Gordon, supported by former Newcastle team-mate Lewis Hall, was a threat throughout. He came close to teeing up an opener while the two sides were still 11 vs 11, but saw Morgan Rogers curl his low cross against the far post on the turn.

Even once Sulc had been dismissed following a VAR review for a studs-up challenge on the shin of Elliot Anderson, it took a reshuffle from Thomas Tuchel and the half-time arrival of Eberechi Eze for many of his team-mates to catch up following a particularly nervous and passive opening period from the Three Lions.

But once they did, it was Gordon who took full advantage less than two minutes after the restart to stoop and turn Trent Alexander-Arnold's typically inviting cross home, netting for the third competitive game in a row.

England ratings Trafford (7), Alexander-Arnold (7), Chalobah (5), Guehi (6), Hall (7), Anderson (6), Lewis-Skelly (6), Saka (5), Rogers (7), Rogers (8), Kane (7).



Subs: Eze (7), Scott (7), Ngumoha (7), Bellingham (6), Gibbs-White (6).

Alexander-Arnold later revealed to ITV: "I spoke to Anthony at half-time and I said if I'm getting in the half spaces and putting them [crosses] in, make sure you get to the back post.

"You don't expect it to happen that quickly, but it did and it worked."

Hall, too, nearly got his just desserts when his dangerous low delivery was turned onto his own post by Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci with Rogers sniffing.

Coincidentally it would be a mix of Rogers and a deflection off Krejci that would tee-up Harry Kane, who else, to sweep home a second with England's next attack to put the result beyond doubt and add his 87th international goal.

Image: Harry Kane added another to his record tally with an 87th international goal to seal victory, his ninth England goal in 11 games in 2026

That gave Tuchel the confidence to give out two competitive debuts to Alex Scott and Rio Ngumoha, both introduced shortly afterwards.

Scott would come within inches of a debut goal while Rogers and Eze both also went lose to adding to England's lead, but the Three Lions would at least see out a comfortable and much-needed win to get their Nations League campaign off the ground at the second attempt.

The key moments from Prague

5: CHANCE! A simple ball over the top is misjudged by Anderson and reaches Sulc, who holds off Trevor Chalobah but is denied by James Trafford when the goalkeeper is quick off his line.

13: SULC AGAIN! Sulc is given space to run in outside the area and is hesitant to take a shot, before eventually seeing an effort blocked by Chalobah's head.

16: OFF THE POST! Out of nothing England nearly strike as Rogers turns on the ball and fires against the far post from Gordon's low cross.

21: CLOSE! Gordon himself goes close next, bending just wide after cutting in off the flank.

25: RED CARD! Having twice gone close for the hosts, Czech player of the year Sulc sees a yellow card upgraded to a red by VAR for a high lunge on Anderson.

38: GORDON DANGER! The flying winger gets beyond his man and whips a low ball in which Michal Sadilek bundles behind, only just beyond his own goalframe.

45: KANE CHANCE! Captain Kane goes close in his first chance of the game, turning and shooting from 20 yards and forcing Matej Kovar into a one-handed stop.

46: SUB! Eze is brought on for Myles Lewis-Skelly at the interval to give England's midfield more attacking threat.

47: GOAL! The Three Lions get their second half off to the perfect start as Alexander-Arnold's wicked cross is headed home by a stooping Gordon.

63: OFF THE POST! Another low cross nearly results in an own goal as Hall's delivery is turned onto his own post by Krejci.

69: GOAL! Rogers and Krejci compete for a loose ball which falls to Kane, who makes no mistake sweeping home into the far corner.

72: SUBS! Kane and Gordon make way to give Ngumoha and Scott their competitive debuts.

87: CHANCE! Scott goes close on debut with a rising effort which flies just over from 20 yards.

Tuchel: We needed more dynamism

England head coach Thomas Tuchel on ITV:

"We played very professionally in the second half. We stepped up, we needed to be a bit more dynamic and put a bit more urgency into our play.

"We kept the intensity going and it was very professional. The effort was still there, it was a deserved victory. It's a bit strange to get an early red card, it's not the best for the spectators or the teams.

"But we got an important win, and that's what counts."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England captain Harry Kane admitted he only found out about Manchester City's charges after the game and that he is only focused on his country at the moment.

Gordon: I've been dying to play with Trent

England goalscorer and man-of-the-match Anthony Gordon on ITV:

"I make that run time and time again and only a certain type of player has got the technique, ability and bravery to make the mistake playing that pass.

"Credit to Trent, that's why he's so good. I've been dying to play with him for that reason.

"Trent's had his own journey with England. He would have liked to have played more than he has but he's a great character. He's a great addition."

Image: Gordon celebrates his goal with Trent Alexander-Arnold

England returnee Trent Alexander-Arnold on ITV:

"It was amazing, always an honour and pleasure to represent my country.

"It's been a long time but I've always believed that I can play for England and I always want to.

"The belief is always there, it's about proving it at club level. The manager gave me the chance tonight to play and to try to follow what he asked of me to the best of my ability. Hopefully he's happy with how I played."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel praised Trent Alexander-Arnold's performance during England's 2-0 win over the Czech Republic.

Analysis: Alexander-Arnold showed what England have been missing

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett in Prague:

"Trent Alexander-Arnold was always going to make the headlines in his first start for two years.

"There was one moment of real class and plenty of other impressive cameos which showed Tuchel - and the England supporters - what they've been missing for so long.

"His curling cross at the start of the second half which pin-pointed Anthony Gordon's head was joyous, as was the gleeful way the Barcelona man scored his third England goal in as many matches. Gordon has really blossomed into one of England's most exciting and important attacking players.

"Overall, England did enough. There will be plenty of fans who will think they should have put Czech Republic to the sword, especially seeing as the home side played for over an hour with 10-men.

"But against the deepest of deep blocks, England worked hard to eventually get the breakthrough and Kane's sharp finish sealed a solid if unspectacular victory.

"There were no obvious injuries, which is a plus. The second of four matches in 11 days won't live long in the memory, but job done for Tuchel."

England's upcoming Nations League Group A3 fixtures

Saturday October 3: Croatia (A), kick-off 5pm

Tuesday October 6: Czech Republic (H), kick-off 7.45pm

Sports.title: Ten-man Scotland beaten by Switzerland in Pocognoli's first home match
Sports.content:
Sebastien Pocognoli tasted defeat in his first match at Hampden as his 10-man Scotland side were comfortably beaten 3-0 by Switzerland in Nations League B.

Defender Jack Hendry was dismissed inside the first 10 minutes for denying a clear goalscoring opportunity when he hauled down Nottingham Forest's Dan Ndoye - before former AC Milan full-back Ricardo Rodriguez carefully curled the resulting free-kick into the top-left corner from the edge of the box.

This followed a period of confusion around the national stadium in which Serb referee Nenad Minakovic had originally awarded a penalty and shown Hendry a yellow card before his decision was corrected by VAR.

Scotland responded well and fought valiantly despite their numerical disadvantage but were eventually foiled early in the second half when Remo Freuler's low cross picked out Nico Elvedi who helped the ball into the far corner at the near post.

Burnley forward Zeki Amdouni then completed the scoring in the 82nd minute by stepping onto Ndoye's cutback and lashing the ball past Scotland stopper Angus Gunn.

The Scots travel to North Macedonia on Saturday then welcome Slovenia to Hampden next Tuesday - still in search of their first victory in Nations League B1.

The key moments from Hampden Park

9: PENALTY TO SWITZERLAND! Hendry brings down Ndoye and the referee points to the spot.

10: NO PENALTY! VAR has taken a look and the challenge was outside the box. But Hendry is sent off.

Image: Jack Hendry was red-carded at 0-0

12: GOAL FOR SWITZERLAND! Well it was not a penalty but what a free-kick! Rodriguez steps up and blasts the ball past Gunn and the Swiss are ahead.

21: SCOTLAND WANT A PENALTY! John McGinn protests that he was being held as the corner is curled in, but it is play on. Andy Robertson then blasts the next corner over the bar.

29: BOOS AROUND HAMPDEN! Oli McBurnie is clipped as he looks to take the ball into the box. Free-kick? No says the referee.

45+1: YELLOW! Pocognoli picks up a booking as he shows his frustration at some of the refereeing decisions.

51: CHANCE! Ndoye sends the ball into the box, but Johan Manzambi cannot get to it in time and it goes past the post.

55: GOAL FOR SWITZERLAND! It is too easy for Switzerland. Elvedi sweeps home Ndoye's cross to double their advantage. Groans around Hampden.

82: GOAL FOR SWITZERLAND! It gets worse for Scotland. Amdouni gets on the end of Ndoye's cross and smashes the ball into the net. A tough night at Hampden Park.

'After eight minutes, game plan had to be put on the side'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli was frustrated as his Hampden Park debut ended in a 3-0 defeat to Switzerland.

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli:

"Frustrating night, to be honest. Not a lot to say about the game, we can analyse the game with 80 per cent of the game with 10 men.

"Direct finish from the red card with a free-kick, so probably the worst situation that we can have.

"Should prefer maybe a penalty and to stay with with 11 men and to maybe show exactly what we what we planned for the game.

"But we start quite aggressive, front foot and after eight minutes the game plan has to put on the side and just see the team reacting well or not with 10 men.

"They did their best, to be honest. They had the great attitude to stick together, try to have the moment in transition or set pieces or something, but it never happened because Switzerland is a good side as well and they didn't give anything away."

'We have to stay positive'

Image: Scotland captain Andy Robertson is dejected

Scotland captain Andy Robertson speaking to BBC Scotland:

"Your first home game under the new manager, you want to get off to a good start.

"It got off to the worst possible start getting a man sent off early doors. It was incredibly hard with 11 men on the pitch, it was even harder with 10.

"We hardly touched the ball second half, but it didn't stop the lads from fighting for each other.

"Football is about split second decisions, Jack Hendry has tried to nick the ball. As soon as the referee said it was outside the box I thought we would have been better taking the penalty and the yellow card.

"It's a difficult night but we won't try and let it get in the way of our process. We've got a new manager and a new squad so we have to try to stay positive.

"Going into the next game we have to try to forget about it.

"I think he [the manager] was proud of the fight that we showed. What we've planned for the last three days went completely out the window. We had to rip up the plan and try something else.

"Ultimately I don't think we'll take too much from this game in terms of how we want to look as a Scotland team.

"It's up to everyone to stay positive. I'm proud of how the camp has gone so far we just need to get the results."

Sports.title: Disguised funding and 'dishonest' witnesses - key revelations from City verdict
Sports.content:
In a damning 40-page document, an independent commission laid bare its findings into Manchester City's breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. Here, Sky Sports takes a look at the key revelations...

Guilty on all serious financial charges

Manchester City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

The charge that was not proven was regarding one element of the Premier League's non-cooperation case.

'Disguised Funding Scheme'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News takes you through a timeline of Manchester City's charge

The independent commission repeatedly concluded that a number of City's commercial agreements were "shams" and "far in excess" of fair market value.

City used a "Disguised Funding Scheme" where Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) partially funded sponsorship fees from Abu Dhabi sponsors.

As a result, the club's financial statements showed their commercial income from Abu Dhabi sponsors was £949.94m from 2009-10 to 2017-18.

In reality, the Abu Dhabi sponsors only paid £119.25m to City over that period, and the remaining £830.69m was paid by ADUG.

"By using the Disguised Funding Scheme at the very end of the 2009/10 financial year", the commission's report read, "the club was able to avoid breaking the record for the largest single-season loss in Premier League history".

It was concluded that City's financial statements for the seasons between 2009/10 and 2017/18 "did not show a true and fair view" of the club's financial position.

The commission's report also mentions three separate remuneration agreements that were omitted from City's accounts and paid for by ADUG that were worth nearly £17m.

City tried to 'obscure' realities of scheme

The commission's report shows how City unsuccessfully argued against the Disguised Funding Scheme.

City said Abu Dhabi sponsors were liable for the amounts stated in their financial reports, but from time to time these sponsors would apply for financial support from the Abu Dhabi government.

The commission rejected City's explanation, which it concluded had been "concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the Disguised Funding Scheme".

The commission used an example of the scheme in action from May 2013.

Faced with falling foul of UEFA's FFP rules following an unexpected shortfall on their books, City generated amended sponsorship agreements that recorded additional Abu Dhabi sponsorship income, despite the sponsors themselves not being approached.

'The Fordham Arrangement'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News has obtained a video of Man City CEO Ferran Soriano that was sent to internal staff and players at the club after the guilty verdict in relation to allegations of serious breaches of financial rules

City used a third party, Fordham, as a device to overstate income by £24.5m and understate expenses by £49.414m.

The commission described 'The Fordham Arrangement' as being "little more than a front for ADUG".

The Fordham Arrangement was, the commission contended, "a further device by which ADUG funds could be paid into the club in a manner that concealed their true origin" and which enabled "the club to remove operating expenses from its financial statements".

The Fordham Arrangement was part of a system called 'Project Longbow' which "was a multi-strand project whose purpose was to explore how the club might boost its revenues and reduce its operating losses".

But while "many of the strands of Project Longbow were genuine, legitimate attempts to achieve those aims. One was not. That was the Fordham Arrangement".

'Dishonest witnesses'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol explains what Man City's penalty could be and when a decision will be made

The independent commission heard factual evidence from 27 witnesses over 42 days in the last quarter of 2024, with a core bundle of key documents running to "many tens of thousands of pages".

The commission says the club made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the investigation.

It also found some witnesses on behalf of the club gave false evidence, while other City witnesses were found by the commission to give knowingly untrue evidence and so had been dishonest.

City 'intended to circumvent PL rules'

The commission found City had breached UEFA and Premier League financial rules, while also ruling that "by its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the PL rules".

The Premier League said it regarded City's conduct as having "extremely serious, significant, sustained and intentional or reckless breaches of rules critical to the proper and fair operation of the Premier League's league competition".

Manchester City have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday October 2 to do so.

Matt Fitzpatrick believes he is currently playing the best golf of his career, ahead of the world No 4 teeing it up alongside his father at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

Fitzpatrick registered a fourth worldwide win of the season with a three-shot victory at the FedEx Open de France on Sunday, having already won three times on the PGA Tour during an impressive campaign.

The Englishman failed to finish higher than 14th in any of the majors in 2026 but still had six worldwide top 10s along with his victories, with Fitzpatrick proud of his season and contending so frequently.

"Obviously that [a disappointing major season] is a disappointment. It's the goal of anyone's at the start of the year to contend in the majors - those are what mean the most and those are what matter.

Sports.title: Manchester City guilty over Premier League charges after £900m of ‘sham’ contracts
Sports.content:
The Premier League has confirmed Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges of breaching its financial rules over a nine-year period, with the club found to have boosted their income by a staggering amount of more than £900m.

In a bombshell announcement the Premier League revealed an independent commission had found City guilty of arranging “sham ­contracts” with commercial partners to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs, and of filing inaccurate accounts to hide the true state of their finances, which if accurately reported would have led to significant breaches of Premier League and Uefa spending limits.

The club were also found to have entered into “sham” image rights deals with players and the then manager Roberto Mancini to artificially inflate their earnings.

City have said they will appeal by Friday’s deadline “on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”. Their chief executive, ­Ferran Soriano, said in a video sent to employees that the decision was based on a “Premier League conspiracy theory”.

The appeal is expected to run alongside a sanctions hearing presided over by the independent commission, with the Premier League eager to conclude matters as quickly as possible.

The extraordinary scale of what Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali, has described as City’s “financial doping” has sent shock waves throughout the world of ­football, leaving executives at other Premier League clubs stunned.

The Premier League’s chief ­executive, Richard Masters, described the case “as the most significant in Premier League history”. It seems inevitable it will lead to an unprecedented punishment, including in all probability a points deduction that will condemn City to relegation.

Although there is no direct precedent given the scale of City’s offences, Everton’s 10-point penalty for breaching profitability and sustainability rules by £19.5m over a period ending with the 2021-22 season was based on a Premier League tariff of six points for the initial breach, plus an additional point for every £5m the club overspent.

The commission made damning comments regarding the behaviour of City witnesses during the hearings. “Evidence given by a number of important factual witnesses called to give evidence on behalf of the club was false in a number of key respects,” it wrote, arguing that some witnesses had given evidence “they knew to be untrue and so had been dishonest”.

City were found to have operated a “disguised funding scheme” worth £830.6m over nine seasons, from 2009-10 to 2017-18, and to have hidden costs by a further £70m. In addition the club have been found guilty of multiple breaches of failing to cooperate with the Premier League and act in good faith. The commission concluded the club had made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the investigation.

The Premier League published a redacted 40-page “core decision” from the independent commission, which has taken almost two years to produce after a 42-day hearing that concluded in December 2024.

The league said: “The independent commission found City arranged ‘sham’ commercial deals with a number of its sponsors during the period, which were part of a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees. The remainder was funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano leaving the European Football Clubs board meeting in Copenhagen. Photograph: PA Video/PA

“As part of the scheme, further ‘sham’ arrangements, funded by ADUG, were entered into to enable the club to record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred, as well as a ‘sham’ circular arrangement with Fordham, an entity that purchased the club’s players’ image rights, that was funded by ADUG.

“The purpose of these schemes was found to have been to artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than £900m during the affected period, to appear to comply with financial rules.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The consequence of this, as the commission found, was that the club filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators.”

Quick Guide How do I 

ADUG bought City on behalf of Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan for £200m in 2008, with the new owners making an immediate impact by paying £32.5m to sign the Brazilian superstar Robinho from Real Madrid. That was the start of a spending spree City struggled to afford from their existing revenues, with the independent commission concluding that the only way to match the owners’ ambitions for the club was for ADUG to “provide very significant funds by way of equity contribution”.

The commission report states that in 2010 City devised a scheme whereby sponsors would pay a “base sum” and ADUG would pay a “tagged sum”, despite the base sum being the only true revenue. The recorded sponsorship fee would be the total of them both.

City’s lawyers claimed that the “tagged sum” was a loan by the Abu Dhabi government on liabilities on sponsorship fees. The commission rejected that argument.

The judgment is a huge victory for the Premier League and Masters. Despite the commission demonstrating that City breached Uefa’s spending limits there appears little prospect of Uefa’s case being revisited because there is a five-year statute of limitations on its disciplinary proceedings. Uefa’s punishment of City in relation to alleged financial fair play breaches was largely overturned in 2020 by the court of arbitration for sport, which found “most of the alleged breaches were either not established or time-barred”.

Masters said: “The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade. It also vindicates the Premier League’s decision to pursue this case against Manchester City.”

He said in relation to sanctions: “Now we have the commission’s decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the league, our clubs and fans.”

Other Premier League clubs are surprised City have not reached an agreed sanction with the Premier League, given the judgment, but City continue to deny wrongdoing. “Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission, that has been published today,” the club said. “The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.”

Sports.title: Gordon and Kane fire England to Nations League victory against 10-man Czechia
Sports.content:
Anybody can lose to Spain. But when England did so at Wembley on Saturday, it served to turn up the temperature for this trip to Czechia. England have form for finding it difficult at this compact stadium. Remember the European Championship qualifier here in 2019 when they lost 2-1?

It was not easy at first. Thomas Tuchel shuffled his pack, making the surprise decision to start Jude Bellingham among the substitutes. It was all a little angsty and Czechia, for whom this is the dawn of a new era under the Spaniard Santi Denia after their World Cup wipeout, dared to dream of another upset.

Then everything changed. It was a rash challenge in the 23rd minute by Pavel Sulc on Elliot Anderson, late and high, albeit nothing overtly nasty. The referee, Umut Meler, showed the Czechia midfielder a yellow card and on we went. Yet the VAR was not happy and when Meler was called to the pitchside monitor, everybody knew what was coming next.

It was a red card to disfigure the contest but Tuchel was not complaining. His players made the most of the decision to get their Nations League campaign up and running with the standout moment being provided by Tuchel’s headline selection.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was in from the cold at the outset for only his second appearance under Tuchel; the first was as a substitute against Andorra in the summer of last year. It was the Real Madrid player who helped to unlock the stalemate at the beginning of the second half, his whipped cross made to measure for Anthony Gordon.

Harry Kane added the second with his 87th England goal and, after all the focus on England’s defensive vulnerability, there was the bonus for Tuchel of a first clean sheet in seven matches. The team had conceded 13 times in the previous six. It did not start particularly well. By the end, it was a stroll.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane fires home to double England’s lead with his 87th goal for the national team. Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock

The inclusion of Alexander-Arnold at right-back was the ­wildcard. Any team with him in it feels more nuanced and it meant Tuchel retained only Marc Guéhi from the back four against Spain. Ezri Konsa and Nico O’Reilly had minor injuries. With Trevoh Chalobah in central defence and Lewis Hall at left-back, it was a completely untested unit.

England lacked cohesion at the outset. There were errors from them and it was easy to fret about their lack of care on the ball; the looseness of some of the passing. They were a little open at the back. Czechia were the better team until the sending-off.

England could highlight the moment on 16 minutes when Gordon took a fizzed pass from Myles Lewis-Skelly and crossed low for Morgan Rogers. The man who came in for Bellingham spun and sent a shot against the inside of the far post. But Czechia had flickers. Sulc almost got in after Anderson misjudged a high ball. Lukas Cerv hit a sweet volley past the post. Sulc choose the wrong option when well-placed and was crowded out by Guéhi and Chalobah.

View image in fullscreen Pavel Sulc (left) is shown a red card by Halil Meler for a foul on Elliot Anderson. Photograph: Slávek Růta/Zuma Press/Shutterstock

The red card was devastating for Sulc, and not only because he did not have to jump into the tackle. It was in a non-threatening area of the pitch for Czechia. He overstretched in an effort to win the ball and it did not feel crazily excessive in terms of the force. There was no outrage from the England players around Anderson. At the monitor, though, Meler concluded that it ticked the boxes for an upgrade to red. As always, it looked worse on the slow-motion replays.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Czechia felt their attacking ambition evaporate. England came to dominate the ball. What could they do with it? Not much before the ­interval. Kane took another incisive pass from Lewis-Skelly and extended Matej Kovar in the 45th minute but that was about it.

Tuchel finished the first half in an almighty funk at the fourth official after a decision had gone against Bukayo Saka. The manager reset at the interval, sending on Eberechi Eze for Lewis-Skelly – who was booked on 35 minutes – and going to a 4-1-4-1. Lewis-Skelly had lunged in on Cerv, whose screams could be heard up in the press box. The Czechs wanted a red card to even things up. It was not that bad but Tuchel could not take any chances.

View image in fullscreen Anthony Gordon plants his astute second-half header, from Trent Alexander-Arnold’s cross, into the corner of the net. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

England got the breakthrough almost immediately and it was one for the Alexander-Arnold lovers. When Czechia coughed up the ball cheaply, he chased it down on the right, turned and did what he does. The pinged cross had a low trajectory and it bounced once before sitting up for Gordon, whose headed conversion was marked by precision. It was deserved reward for Gordon, who was quick and urgent; the player most likely to spark England.

England relaxed. They were good thereafter. Hall began to surge up the line. He shot inches wide after getting a pass back from Gordon while he watched Ladislav Krejci turn a low cross from him against the far post. The Kane goal was inevitable and it came when he drilled a loose ball into the far corner after a break into the box by Rogers.

Tuchel got Alex Scott on for his debut and he did well. Ditto Rio ­Ngumoha, who also came off the bench. England might have scored more with Kovar making a particularly fine save to deny Eze. Next up for them is Croatia away on Saturday.

Sports.title: Switzerland’s Rodríguez and Elvedi punish Scotland after Hendry’s early red card
Sports.content:
Switzerland have responded exceptionally well after allegations of capers involving vaccination certificates that threatened to overshadow this international window. Make that six points out of six for Murat Yakin’s stylish team. Switzerland look comfortably capable of breezing out of Group B1 in the Nations League. They have not even played at home yet. Granit who?

Sébastien Pocognoli, conversely, has been left to ponder one step forward and umpteen back. Scotland’s second half in Slovenia at the ­weekend provided hope to the new manager and a supporter base who want to enter a brave new world. Age old, troublesome flaws remain.

Jack Hendry’s red card meant Scotland played almost 80 minutes of this encounter with 10 men. They were, however, outclassed in every department. Scottish patterns of play were not immediately obvious. The upcoming trip to North Macedonia carries importance as Pocognoli seeks to win hearts and minds. This was all pretty grim for anyone of a Scotland persuasion.

“The red card of Jack is all of our red card,” said Pocognoli. “We stay together. We put this moment in our DNA today and hopefully it can be helpful for the future.”

Scottish expectancy heading into a World Cup where they subsequently took tedium to new levels feels a long time ago. They have scored only once in five games. Impotence can only concern Scotland’s Belgian manager, whose bow at Hampden Park was over as a contest long before full-time. A penny for the thoughts of Steve Clarke, Pocognoli’s immediate predecessor and a coach much-maligned in certain quarters. Were Clarke in charge of this ragged display, the public response would have been ferocious.

Judgment of Pocognoli on this occasion requires appropriate context. Switzerland had control of the early exchanges without creating anything until a slick move saw Dan Ndoye sent through on goal from the halfway line. It was quickly apparent ­Hendry did not have the pace to halt his ­opponent. Initially, the referee Nenad Minakovic booked Hendry and awarded a penalty for the clear pull on Ndoye which ­toppled the Swiss forward. Following a video assistant referee check that was unnecessarily lengthy, the official corrected his decision to a free-kick and sending off. Up stepped Ricardo Rodríguez to crack the ball beyond Angus Gunn from 19 yards.

Pocognoli’s immediate response was to withdraw Kieron Bowie, one of two strikers. The introduction of ­Stephen Welsh retained Scotland’s three-man backline. A noticeably subdued Hampden crowd feared a long evening. This is, after all, a Switzerland team that followed up a strong World Cup performance with a comfortable win in North Macedonia on Saturday.

John McGinn appealed in vain for a penalty after claiming he was held at a Scotland corner. The blunt truth is Scotland have needed more from McGinn than the seeking or winning of fouls for some time.

McGinn’s Aston Villa teammate Johan ­Manzambi was unsurprisingly lively; he fired just wide of Gunn’s right-hand post moments after a delicious cross that found no Swiss takers. With half an hour played, the Scots were gasping for air against opponents who looked physically and technically superior. When in possession, far too much of the hosts’ play was sideways or backwards. Gunn denied Ndoye nine minutes before the break.

View image in fullscreen Nico Elvedi celebrates after doubling Switzerland’s lead from close range in the second half. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

The half ended with a yellow card for Pocognoli, who protested a little too vociferously after McGinn was fouled. All the episode did was sum up Scottish frustration. There had been needle in the game but the coherent football had been played by those in red.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Manzambi had irritated the home support by embellishing fouls and entering into a verbal spat with Oli McBurnie. His play, though, was a compelling watch. Manzambi’s movement unnerved Scotland. His willingness to drop deep or wide to get involved in the game emphasised his versatility. His touch and dribbling ability set him apart; all at the age of 20. Scotland’s lack of anything approaching such emerging talent is glaring.

Switzerland’s second came from a more unlikely source. Scotland only partially cleared a corner, with the ball funnelled wide right to Ndoye. The cross was pacy and low, with the central defender Nico Elvedi striding forward to flick home. Two nil was a more appropriate reflection of events to that point.

Pocognoli now made a triple change. McBurnie’s 18th cap had passed without the ending of his international scoring wait. As on Saturday, the alterations were like-for-like in positional nature. ­Pocognoli’s level of tactical flexibility remains open to question. Yakin withdrew ­Manzambi, in what could be classed as a humanitarian act towards Scotland.

Not that Switzerland had stopped dishing out punishment. The ­closing stages resembled an attack ­versus defence training exercise. A third from the Swiss was inevitable as they toyed with the Scots.

Gunn was pitifully weak in attempting to deal with Zeki ­Amdouni’s strike, which flew into the roof of the Scotland net via the goalkeeper. Cue a mass exodus from the stands. Pocognoli has been served a strong, painful reminder of the scale of task he chose to inherit.

Sports.title: Nations League roundup: Lamine Yamal sinks Croatia in Spain’s World Cup homecoming
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League in their first home game since lifting the World Cup.

Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring within two minutes against England in Saturday’s Wembley win and took just 75 seconds to do so against Slaven Bilic’s side in Andalusia. The teenager’s left-footed finish took his tally of international goals to nine in 36 appearances.

Just before the half-hour mark, the visitors equalised through Dion Beljo’s header as the 6ft 4in attacker headed home from an Ivan Perisic cross.

Two minutes later the hosts restored their lead as Marc Pubill fired home a header from a pinpoint Lamine Yamal cross before provider turned scorer again on 63 minutes, beating Barcelona teammate and Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic at his near post. With fewer than two minutes to play Athletic Bilbao’s Nico Williams notched up a fourth for Spain with a crisp dribble and finish.

La Roja next play Czechia on Saturday in Group A3.

Lamine Yamal’s contribution strengthened his case for the Ballon d’Or, with voting having closed on Monday and the winner announced on 26 October.

Spain’s captain, Rodri, showed off the World Cup trophy before kick-off at the packed Estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, being handed it by Sevilla legend Jesús Navas, a winner with Spain in 2010.

“We were very excited to bring the cup here,” Lamine Yamal said. “To be able to win the game and bring it home is great.”
